F3.evidence: No artefact-level metadata record exists to carry an identifier (Row 6: F3 = 0 for supplement-only deposits).

F4.evidence: Supplement is not indexed as a resource in a searchable registry (Row 6: F4 = 0). The upstream ADS dataset is DataCite-indexed, but it is non-principal: the paper's revised model, not the ADS archive, is what reproduction requires.

I1.evidence: The principal data are expressed as an OxCal model: 'The revised chronological model was implemented in OxCal ... It comprises two sections; the first defines the likelihoods and their constraints, and the second defines occurrences for each of the bead types' (l. 267-270). OxCal's Chronological Query Language (CQL) is a formal, documented, shared, machine-parseable representation. Caveat: the container file format is not stated in the paper.

I2.evidence: Bead types follow an expert classification ('bead identifications by an expert (Nielsen, 2013) according to an established classification (Brugmann, 2004)', l. 225-227; codes such as BE1-Dghnt). No PID-bearing or FAIR controlled vocabulary (e.g. PeriodO, Getty AAT) is cited.

I3.evidence: The derived data carry a qualified PID reference to their source: the chronological prior is taken from 'the OxCal model deposited in the project archive (Hines, 2013)' (l. 233-234), and the reference list types the source as '[data-set]. Archaeological Data Service. https://doi.org/10.5284/1018290'. The pack confirms that the DOI resolves at DataCite (state findable).

R1.evidence: The paper describes the dataset's composition and attributes in detail: 72 female graves (52 from Hines & Bayliss 2013 plus 20 from Lakenheath, l. 212-219), the two-section model structure, the retained stratigraphic and artefact constraints (Castledyke, Dover Buckland, Edix Hill, Melbourn; BU2-d/h after AD 510; Dagobert I coin after AD 629, l. 237-247), and 23 bead types (Fig. 4).

R1_1.evidence: No separate supplement licence is stated, so the supplement takes the same licence as the paper (R1.1 rule (a)). Two article licences are identifiable: the source PDF cover page says 'Article available under the terms of the CC-BY-NC-ND licence', and the pack's Crossref record lists the Elsevier user licence (https://www.elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0/) plus Elsevier policy URIs. Under the most-restrictive rule the Elsevier user licence governs. That is still a clear, accessible licence with stated terms, not 'ask permission'.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance is given. The prior derives from the Bayliss et al. (2013) model in the Hines (2013) archive, and three named constraints were removed with reasons ('(i) a sequence that models all the radiocarbon dates ... (ii) a sequence based on non-overlapping occurrences of bead-types ... (iii) a combined age determination for two burials, MaDE1 and MaDE2', l. 248-260). Lakenheath graves were added (Hines 2021). The paper also states 'calibrates with OxCal version 4.4.2 and the IntCal20 calibration curve' (l. 270-271) and 'five independent runs of the model indicate negligible between-run variability' (l. 272-273).

R1_3.evidence: The principal artefact is a publisher supplement with no deposit-level metadata standard (DataCite, Dublin Core, or domain schema). The IntCal20/OxCal methodological standards do not qualify. The ADS route-(c) entitlement applies only to the upstream, non-principal Hines (2013) archive, not to the paper's own data.
